takeaway: A Krukenberg tumour is an ovarian metastasis, most often from gastric carcinoma. Think stomach when histology shows a Krukenberg tumour.

question.text: A 76-year-old woman has a peritonitic abdomen. At laparotomy a pelvic mass is biopsied and histology suggests a Krukenberg tumour. Which is the most likely primary source?

lines.text: This woman has a pelvic mass, found during her emergency laparotomy.
Histology shows a Krukenberg tumour: a secondary deposit in the ovary, full of signet ring cells.
So the real question is, where did it come from?
Classically it comes from the stomach, a gastric carcinoma, spreading to the ovary.
Gastric cancer often presents late, which is why spread like this is seen.
Pancreas, lung and breast cancer can spread too, but they are not the classic source.
